header.title: Connection tokens
header.subtitle: Time-limited credentials for connecting through the proxy. Tokens always expire — there are no permanent secrets.

modes.oneShotBody: Generate a token and paste it as the password in psql / mysql / DataGrip. It stops working when it expires; generate a new one next time.
modes.brokerBody: Run pmon login — the daemon holds your token and opens a local port per datasource; pmon show prints the connection string. Point your client at it with the password pmon show prints, which never changes. The daemon re-mints the token silently; when the session window closes it stops renewing and asks you to run pmon login again.

empty.title: No tokens yet.
empty.hint: Generate a connection token, or run the pmon CLI to mint one.

directConnect.title: Connect a SQL client directly
directConnect.intro: pmon is the recommended path — it brokers a short-lived token and pins the proxy's certificate for you. Connect directly when you would rather point psql, mysql, or DataGrip at the proxy yourself.
directConnect.noneConnectable: You have no datasources you may connect to.
directConnect.noAddress: This datasource's proxy has not advertised a client-facing address yet.
directConnect.tlsOn: Enabled — download the certificate and point your client at it.
directConnect.tlsSystemTrust: Enabled. This proxy uses a publicly trusted certificate and publishes none, so your client verifies it against its own trust store — no certificate file needed.
directConnect.tlsOff: Not enabled on this proxy. A direct connection would be unencrypted, so use pmon on a trusted network instead.
directConnect.rotationNote: Rotating the proxy's certificate invalidates a downloaded copy — download it again after a rotation.
directConnect.verifyModeNote: verify-full checks the certificate and that it covers the address you dialed. If your certificate does not cover that address (no matching hostname or IP SAN), fall back to verify-ca — it still verifies the certificate, only not the identity.
directConnect.datagripHelp: In DataGrip: Data Sources → your connection → SSH/SSL → Use SSL, set CA file to the downloaded certificate and Mode to {mode}.
